newsitem.title: USA: Emerging markets debt rises in very thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Emerging markets debt rises in very thin trading.

text.p: Emerging market debt rose modestly in very light trading on Friday, nudged higher by a rise in U.S. Treasuries, traders said.
"It's been extremely quiet -- you've got your Friday summer doldrums," one trader said.
Spreads over Treasuries turned in a mixed performance, with Ecuador and Bulgaria tightening markedly but several countries widening a touch.
In late trading, Ecuador discounts were up 3/4 at 71-1/2, tightening about 20 basis points.

Buyers stepped in on Friday after heavy selling on Thursday, when Ecuador Finance Minister Carlos Davalos tendered his resignation. As of late Friday, President Fabian Alarcon had not announced whether he would accept the resignation.
"Ecuador Bradies got pummelled yesterday and today we saw people step back in, cover some shorts, that type of thing," a trader said.
Traders again mentioned speculation that Venezuela may be preparing to refinance some of its Brady debt, but they said the rumors had little bearing on prices.
"There's speculation about a 30-year Venezuela bond and that the proceeds are going to buy back some Bradies," one trader said.
"We certainly believe that's a legitimate possibility in the future," he added.
Venezuela Bradies were mixed, with pars up 1/4 at 79 but discounts off 3/8 at 88-1/4.
More broadly, Brazil "C" bonds were up 5/8 at 80-3/4, Argentina FRBs were up 1/8 at 93-3/4 and Mexico pars were up 3/8 at 77-1/2.
